assertions.name: requires an explicit date and review, labels all inputs and reads once in StrictMode
persists before send and retries the same request after a lost reply and remount
cancels an unresolved request with the original payload and displays cancellation without a saved date
reports an already saved result when cancellation arrives after commit
clears review after editing and refuses to write without storage or a browser lock
retains a mismatched success receipt and an uncertain replay after access loss
releases only a definite initial refusal and requires a new read
ignores late success after another tab changes the held request
keeps admin read-only and corrupted recovery closed
parses the actual PostgreSQL model workspace, source selection and stored result
refuses malformed fields, boolean coercion, duplicate source identities and inconsistent cursors
requires real calendar dates and finite exact version strings
refuses unreviewed, unauthorized, unobserved and wrong-actor commands
refuses a success that changes request, actor, effective date, source, version or reason
keeps the durable request until its exact verified reply can be retired
cancels with the original request and payload, without inventing a saved policy id or version
retains malformed, changed and wrong-actor storage instead of overwriting or clearing it
uses the two literal RPCs and preserves server errors for safe initial-refusal handling

targeted_repairs: The two recovery scenarios were checked; then the accessory save and stale-version scenarios were checked against their corrected scope. Unaffected successful assertions were retained.
